summary:
Batch.scheduleWith (FS.GG.Coord.Core) admits work for parallel workers as a greedy independent set over a touch-set conflict graph, walked in Rank order.

- Rank.key is a lexicographic total order: starvation escalation, blocking count (whole-board Blocked-by graph), Severity, Class, Phase, age, then issue number. The number term keeps the batch deterministic on identical input, so two workers reading one cached window compute one batch.
- Rank aging: a Ready item at least StarvationDays = 21 days old escalates above every other term, so a wide-touch item cannot starve forever. An unread input is the lowest tier and never promotes.
- Each candidate is admitted if it clears everything already reserved, so the top-ranked schedulable item is always in the batch. Total parallelism may drop versus a maximal pack; displacedBy and explainRanking report it.
- Held items reserve their touch-set. A reservation with an unmatchable touch-set fails closed and refuses the whole batch (Red verdict): unschedulable beats mis-scheduled.
- implementerSlots counts occupied slots from claim markers only; work without a claim is reported separately.

Generic technique: list scheduling with a conflict predicate (ADR-0098 OR5) over a maximal independent set. ADR-0098 §11 tranche 2 (FS-GG/.github#5245) lists this record; the generic technique is a pack entry, the FS-GG instance stays here (§10).
title: Conflict-free batch admission: priority-greedy independent set with rank aging
